newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks finish weaker on political jitters.
newsitem.headline: French stocks finish weaker on political jitters.

text.p: French stocks slipped on Friday amid political jitters triggered by a poll suggesting a close parliamentary race between the Socialists and Conservatives.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 3.57 points, or 0.14 percent, at 2,536.26. The index closed down 0.44 percent.
The markets were under pressure from an IPSOS poll released on Thursday afternoon showed the Conservatives with a razor-thin majority.
An IFOP poll is expected to be released at the weekend and Le Figaro is expected to publish a Sofres poll on Monday.
"What the market wants to see is a clear majority for the Conservatives to have more certainty they'll win," a trader said.

He said the market would get a big boost from polls giving the Conservatives 310 to 320 seats, compared with 292 seats shown in the IPSOS poll. "But I don't think we'll get that in these polls. It's going to be a very close race," he said.
French pharmaceutical shares staged an early rally on takeover speculation fuelled by reports that Swiss drug giant Roche Holding was issuing $1 billion in convertible bonds.

Shares in Synthelabo and Sanofi jumped in early trading but finished off their highs as analysts said Roche was probably launching the issue to take advantage of cheap liquidity and was not preparing for a takeover.
Synthelabo, controlled by cosmetics group L'Oreal, finished up 1.98 percent at 670 francs.
Shares in Sanofi, controlled by oil major Elf Aquitaine, ended up 2.51 percent at 530 francs.
Elsewhere activity was thin. Volume totalled 4.74 billion francs, with 3.6 billion in the CAC-40 issues.

Eurotunnel shares rose 2.31 percent to 6.65 francs. Eurotunnel said on Thursday it had clinched an agreement with lead banks to restructure its debt, a deal which it said would make it financially secure for the next six years.
